subject: jewel beetle
title: This Beetle Fell in Love With a Beer Bottle, and It Won an Award

scenes.text: Male beetles in Australia keep choosing the wrong partner. It's made of glass.
Scientists found them clinging to brown beer bottles thrown away by the road.
Put a fresh bottle down, and males turned up within thirty minutes.
Brown wine bottles of a different shade? Not one beetle.
Why? The bottle's shiny brown glass and tiny bumps look like a giant, perfect female.
Some males wouldn't let go, even as the sun and ants got them. Killed by a beer bottle.

description:
In Western Australia, male jewel beetles (Julodimorpha bakewelli) were found trying to mate with discarded brown 'stubby' beer bottles. The glass colour and dimpled surface look like an oversized female.
The 1983 study by Darryl Gwynne and David Rentz won the 2011 Ig Nobel Prize in Biology. Some males stayed on the bottles until heat or ants killed them.
What human litter do you think fools the most animals?
first_comment: The bottles all had a bumpy band of glass near the base, exactly what a female's shell looks like to a male. What's the strangest thing you've seen an animal fall for?
